samples.text:
The diagram shows how the rainwater is collected and used in a house. There are seven stages in the process. The diagram have a picture of a house with a garden and a tank under it.

Firstly, rain falls on the roof of the house and runs off the roof surface. Then the water goes into the gutters and the downpipe, which channel it from the edge of roof. After that, the water pass through a leaf filter, so leaves and debris are removed.

Next, the filtered water is stored in a underground tank. The tank is below the garden. When the house needs water, a pump sends the water into the house. The water is used for toilets, washing machine and for watering the garden.

Finally, when the tank is full, the extra water drains to a soakaway. This is the last stage in the diagram. Overall, the process starts with rain on the roof and ends with using the water in the house, and there is also a overflow for the water that the tank cannot keep.
samples.why: Overview present but late and simple · all seven stages covered in order · mechanical linking and some repetition · adequate vocabulary · several article and agreement errors that do not block meaning.

samples.text:
The diagram explains how rainwater is collected from the roof of a house and then used inside the building and in the garden.

Overall, the system involves seven stages, beginning with rainfall on the roof and leading to household use of the stored water. There is also an overflow, which deals with excess water when the tank is full, and the underground tank acts as the central point between collection and use.

First, rain runs off the surface of the roof and is channelled from the roof edge by gutters into a downpipe. The water then passes through a leaf filter, where leaves and other debris are removed, before it is stored in a underground tank located beneath the garden.

When water is needed, it is pumped from the tank into the house. This means that the tank only supplies water to the house when it is actually required. There, it is used for three main purposes: flushing toilets, running the washing machine and watering the garden. Finally, if the tank becomes full, any excess water is drained away to a soakaway rather than stay in the system.
samples.why: Clear overview identifying start, main use and overflow · logical sequencing with passive forms · some less common vocabulary (channelled, debris) · mostly error-free with two minor slips.

samples.text:
The diagram depicts a domestic rainwater harvesting system, showing how rain falling on a house is captured, filtered, stored and eventually put to use.

The process consists of seven stages, starting with rainfall on the roof and culminating in the use of the water within the household, while a separate overflow route handles any surplus once the storage tank has reached capacity.

Rain initially runs off the roof surface and is channelled from its edge into gutters and a downpipe. From there, it passes through a leaf filter designed to trap leaves and debris, and the filtered water is then stored in an underground tank buried beneath the garden.

Whenever water is required, it is pumped from this tank into the house, where it serves three purposes: flushing toilets, supplying the washing machine and watering the garden. Should the tank become full, however, the excess water is not retained; instead, it drains away to a soakaway. In this way, the system both makes use of rainwater and prevents surplus water from building up once storage is exhausted.
samples.why: Well-placed overview covering the main route and overflow · stages logically and fluently linked · precise vocabulary (culminating, capacity, retained) · wide range of structures including inversion · error-free.
